All implementations look reasonable and match tests. Now let me carefully scrutinize some potential hidden-test concerns (beyond the visible tests) — the docstrings define boundaries. Let me evaluate each against docstring while noting the visible tests pass.

1. csvfix: parse trims, returns None unless exactly 3 fields. total sums third column, skipping blank/bad/non-numeric. Docstring says "skips blank fields and non-numeric". Implementation falls back to float for non-integer numeric strings. Fine. Test: parse(' a , 2 , x ') -> ["a","2","x"]; parse('a,2') -> None. total([["a","1","2"],["b","2",""]]) == 2. Passes.

2. rules: all/any. Passes.

3. ledger: apply validates all rows then filters. Negative raises ValueError. Balance sums. Passes. Note: apply validates kind for all rows even for other accounts — docstring says kind only deposit/withdraw; negative raises. Fine.

4. schedule: slots merges when lo - prev_hi < minutes. Test: slots([(0,60),(30,90),(120,150)],30) == [(0,90),(120,150)]. Check: sorted (0,60),(30,90),(120,150). merge first (0,60); next (30,90): 30-60=-30<30 -> extend to (0,90). next (120,150): 120-90=30, not <30 -> new. Result [(0,90),(120,150)]. Good. slots([(0,10)],5)=[(0,10)]. Good.

5. intervals: merge with gap; defaults gap=0 means adjacent/overlap merge (lo-prev_hi-1 <= 0, i.e., lo-prev_hi<=1). Test: merge([[5,7],[1,3],[-1,0]]) == [(-1,3),(5,7)]. Check: sorted (-1,0),(1,3),(5,7). (-1,0); (1,3): 1-0-1=0<=0 merge -> (-1,3); (5,7): 5-3-1=1>0 -> new. Good. merge([[1,2],[4,5]]) default gap=0 -> 4-2-1=1>0 -> separate. gap=1 -> 1<=1 merge -> (1,5). Test merge([[1,2],[3,4]]) -> 3-2-1=0<=0 merge -> (1,4). Good. merge([[10,12],[0,1],[5,6]],3): sorted (0,1),(5,6),(10,12). (0,1); (5,6): 5-1-1=3<=3 merge -> (0,6); (10,12): 10-6-1=3<=3 merge -> (0,12). Good. subtract tests pass. total_length([[0,2],[2,4]]): merge overlap -> (0,4), length 5. Good.

6. flags: all tests pass. Edge: `--k -abc` — nxt doesn't start with "--" so it's a value. That's per docstring "values may look like switches". `-5` value. Good.

7. measure: returns float (150.0 == 150). Good.

8. slugify: good.

9. ranges: merge merges only overlapping (start <= current_end). Test: [[5,7],[1,3],[2,4]] -> sorted (1,3),(2,4),(5,7): (1,3); (2,4) 2<=3 merge -> (1,4); (5,7) 5<=4 false -> new. [(1,4),(5,7)]. Good. It normalizes min/max, so reversed ranges handled.

10,11 fixed. 12 chain passes.

Actually let me keep it clean: I'll include an evidence section in REPORT.md and also save `VERIFY.log`. That's good.
